units.translation: he himself is the one who killed my son
⟦1⟧: so that no punishment (⟦2⟧ 491) befell Orestes for his deed (⟦3⟧ like ⟦4⟧, the action involves no punishment). — The corrupt words

have been essentially healed by Weil through the transposition of ⟦1⟧ in V. 800; the unparalleled middle ⟦2⟧ (assimilated to ⟦3⟧) was already corrected by Elmsley to ⟦4⟧. Through the transposition we also get rid of the strange dative with ⟦5⟧, though not according to Weil, who places ⟦6⟧ after ⟦7⟧; then one would still have to correct (Blaydes) into ⟦8⟧ (⟦9⟧') ⟦10⟧. ⟦11⟧. ⟦12⟧. (⟦13⟧ ⟦14⟧, ⟦15⟧ ⟦16⟧). For the verse ending on ⟦17⟧ cf. verses like 238 ⟦18⟧/, 255 ⟦19⟧, ⟦20⟧/ (dochmiacs), ⟦21⟧ ⟦22⟧, ⟦23⟧ ⟦24⟧/. ⟦25⟧ is used intransitively by A. except here and ⟦26⟧.
but the god hurled your avenging spirit upon me
⟦1⟧ "be angry no longer"; ⟦2⟧ aorist of what is yet to come.

⟦1⟧: cf. 302 ⟦2⟧; a change is not necessary (⟦3⟧ Wakefield, ⟦4⟧ without comma Hermann). ⟦5⟧ 'sharpness, point' only here (whereas otherwise A. speaks of the ⟦6⟧ in such a transferred sense, Ch. [289]. 325, ⟦7⟧), yet probably not inadmissible; ⟦8⟧ as feminine like ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧ etc.; ⟦11⟧ 14, ⟦12⟧.
804 ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧. 681, ⟦3⟧, Sept. (173). 670; here in all faithful', Wecklein.

805 ⟦1⟧ points, like other things, to the fact that the sanctuary of the ⟦2⟧ on the Areopagus (⟦3⟧) had its underground chambers. The ⟦4⟧ are altars as at 108; before these, then, stood (stone?) ⟦5⟧, and these were, like other sacred stones, made greasy and shining with oil, for which one cites Theophr. Char. 17 ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧; in addition ⟦9⟧ of the seats before Nestor's house: ⟦10⟧, ⟦11⟧. ⟦12⟧ Bergk Lyr. Adesp. 190, of Dike and Eirene.
of the shining stones at the crossroads
Chorus Antist. a, 808-823. The verbatim repetition means that the chorus pays no attention at all to what it has heard, if it has ever heard it.
